RM+gamma had gamma silently dropped. Diagnosis: PackTile with TileOffset::Unset emits pack_tile<out_of_order_output=false>, which ignores out_idx and uses an internal sequential counter; the reconfig fold elides the pack reconfig for a second chain packing to the SAME CB, so the counter never rewinds. what: ReduceWithinTile::Skip is UNREACHABLE through compute_kernel_lib::reduce(). The "Skip is AccumulateViaAdd-only" static_assert sits AFTER the `if constexpr (resolved_algorithm == AccumulateViaAdd) { ... return; }` block, so it is not inside a discarded statement and fires for the AccumulateViaAdd instantiation too. Meanwhile reduce_helpers_compute.hpp:158-221 documents Skip at length as THE idiom for summing gathered per-core REDUCE_ROW partials — which is exactly the cross-core combine every normalization op needs. Nothing in the tree uses it, so the breakage is invisible until you try. Cost a design deviation (I fused the collapse into the root combine and shipped raw per-column partials instead).
suggest: Move that static_assert into an `else` branch (or gate it on `resolved_algorithm != AccumulateViaAdd`), and add a kernel_lib unit test that instantiates <AccumulateViaAdd, ..., Skip> so the path stays compiled.

what: A PackTile with caller-managed (ReservePolicy::None, PushPolicy::None) and TileOffset::Unset SILENTLY DROPS its output when a previous chain already packed to the same CB. Reason (only findable in chain.inl:1035-1056): Unset selects pack_tile<out_of_order_output=false>, whose LLK path ignores out_idx and uses an internal sequential counter that is rewound only by a pack reconfig — and the chain reconfig fold elides that reconfig when consecutive chains share a pack CB. So the FIRST in-place chain works and the SECOND writes past the block. No error, no hang; with a constant second operand it is completely invisible (my gamma-of-ones test passed while gamma was being discarded). The public header documents TileOffset::Set as an addressing convenience, never as a correctness requirement.
suggest: In chain.hpp's TileOffset docs state: for (None,None) output policies TileOffset::Set (base 0) is REQUIRED whenever another chain may have packed to the same CB first. Better, make PackTile with (None,None) default to out_of_order_output=true, or static_assert Offset!=Unset for that policy pair.

what: The in-place hazard note (which op_design.md cites as the authority) covers only CB self-deadlock for a SINGLE in-place chain with front-advancing policies. It does not cover the case a real op actually needs: TWO back-to-back chains on one caller-held CB window with (None,None) everywhere. There the CB handshake is absent by construction, so nothing orders chain N's pack against chain N+1's unpack of the same tile. The dst-sync window bounds the skew to ~2 tiles, so it only corrupts when B*S <= 2 — it passed --dev and failed production on exactly the narrow-W / single-tile-row shapes. I had to hand-build the edge (a push/wait round trip on a private 1-page CB, since cb_reserve_back/cb_push_back are PACK-only and cb_wait_front/cb_pop_front UNPACK-only).
suggest: Extend that test file with a two-consecutive-in-place-chains case at n=1 and n=2, and document the sync idiom (or ship it as a kernel_lib helper, e.g. compute_kernel_lib::sync_pack_to_unpack).

what: ttnn.div_up, ttnn.round_up and ttnn.find_max_divisor are documented (with examples and a summary table row each) but are NOT bound in ttnn on this build — hasattr is False for all three. ttnn.tile_size / get_l1_alignment / get_dram_alignment / grid_to_cores / split_work_to_cores do exist. Also device.l1_size_per_core(), which op_design.md and l1_ledger.md both spell as the L1 budget query, is not bound to Python (it exists only on the C++ IDevice), so the budget has to fall back to a named constant.
suggest: Either bind div_up/round_up/find_max_divisor/l1_size_per_core, or mark them C++-only in the reference and show the Python fallback.

what: Two traps that silently invalidate an A/B measurement and are documented nowhere. (1) The ops_perf_results CSV's CORE COUNT column is wrong for a generic op: it reported 56 for a run whose program provably used 11 cores (I proved which process ran by writing TT_METAL_DEVICE_PROFILER into a side file). Ranking variants by it is a false signal. (2) Under --profile the real run executes inside `python -m tracy` and an ad-hoc env var does NOT reach that child, while the precompile warm pass DOES see it — so an env-selected variant measures the warm pass' geometry and the profiled run's default, i.e. the same variant twice with different labels. Compounding it, ttnn caches the compiled program per shape, so a pytest-parametrized A/B of two variants of one shape in one process also silently reuses the first program. Roughly an hour lost chasing identical numbers.
suggest: In perf-measure: warn that CORE COUNT is unreliable for GenericOpDeviceOperation (verify geometry from the host-side plan instead), and state the A/B rule — one process per variant, variant selected by a FILE or a separate test file, never an env var under --profile and never a parametrize within one process.
